- Includes Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements:
  - Note 1—Organization and Operation: American Water is a holding company with regulated utilities providing water/wastewater services in 16 U.S. states (“Regulated Businesses”) and Market-Based Businesses:
    - Homeowner Services Group (HOS): warranty protection and home services to residential customers.
    - Military Services Group (MSG): long-term contracts to operate water/wastewater systems on U.S. military installations.
  - Note 2—Significant Accounting Policies:
    - Regulation: Utilities are regulated by PUCs; application of rate-regulated accounting, including recognition of regulatory assets and liabilities tied to recoverable/ refundable amounts; PUC oversight of revenues, returns, financing, O&M, capex, taxes, affiliated transactions, and corporate actions.
    - Use of Estimates: Management’s critical estimates include regulatory assets/liabilities, revenue recognition (including unbilled revenue), income taxes, benefit plan assumptions, and loss contingencies.
    - Principles of Consolidation: Consolidation of the parent and all subsidiaries with a controlling interest; elimination of intercompany items.
    - Property, Plant and Equipment: Utility plant capitalization practices (materials, labor, indirect costs, AFUDC); repairs and minor replacements expensed; straight-line, group-method depreciation aligned with PUC-approved useful lives.

top5_chunks.title: Selected Financial Data.
top5_chunks.summary:
- Section covered: Item 6, Selected Financial Data from Best Buy’s Form 10-K, presenting five-year financial highlights (2013–2017; 2016 is an 11‑month fiscal year) to be read with MD&A (Item 7) and Financial Statements (Item 8).
- Income statement highlights: Revenue remained relatively stable around $39–41 billion; operating income improved to $1.85 billion in 2017 (operating margin 4.7% vs. 3.5% in 2016); net earnings from continuing operations rose to $1.21 billion in 2017 after weaker prior years (2013 showed a loss).
- Discontinued operations: Small gains/losses across the period; total net earnings attributable to shareholders reached $1.23 billion in 2017.
- Per-share data: EPS from continuing operations increased to $3.74 in 2017; total diluted EPS reached $3.81; cash dividends rose steadily (from $0.66 in 2013 to $1.57 in 2017); stock price range expanded (2017 high $49.40, low $26.10).
- Operating metrics: Comparable sales modestly positive in 2015–2017 (0.3–0.5%) after declines in 2013–2014; gross profit rate improved to 24.0% in 2017; SG&A rate around 19–20%; operating margin strengthened.
- Balance sheet and liquidity: Current ratio near 1.4–1.5; total assets about $13.9 billion in 2017; debt declined from $2.29 billion (2013) to $1.37 billion (2017); total equity $4.71 billion in 2017.
- Footprint: Continued rationalization of stores and space—total stores fell from 1,779 (2013–2014) to 1,575 (2017), with notable reduction internationally; retail square footage declined correspondingly.
- Notable item: 2017 results include $161 million ($100 million net of tax) from CRT and LCD litigation settlements, affecting net earnings; referenced to Note 12, Contingencies and Commitments.

top5_chunks.title: Market for Registrant's Common Equity, Related Stockholder Matters and Issuer Purchases of Equity Securities.
top5_chunks.summary:
- Covers Item 5 (Market for Registrant’s Common Equity, Related Stockholder Matters and Issuer Purchases of Equity Securities) and Item 6 (Selected Financial Data) in Part II of a Form 10-K for Best Buy (ticker: BBY, NYSE).
- Dividends: Regular quarterly cash dividend initiated in 2004 and paid every quarter since; special dividends paid in early fiscal 2016 and fiscal 2017; on March 1, 2017, the regular quarterly dividend was increased 21% to $0.34 per share. Dividend policy remains subject to earnings, capital needs, and other factors. Quarter-by-quarter stock price highs/lows and dividends for fiscal 2016–2017 are provided.
- Stockholders: 2,566 holders of record as of March 20, 2017.
- Share repurchases: Original $5.0 billion authorization from June 2011 (no expiration). In fiscal 2017, 21.1 million shares were repurchased and retired for $0.8 billion; $2.2 billion remained available at year-end. In February 2017, a new $5.0 billion authorization superseded the 2011 plan; on March 1, 2017, the company announced intent to repurchase $3 billion over the next two years. Detailed Q4 fiscal 2017 activity: 5.14 million shares repurchased at an average $43.35; authorization remaining declined from $2.5 billion to $2.238 billion.
- Comparative performance: A five-year cumulative total shareholder return graph (not deemed soliciting or “filed” material) compares BBY to the S&P 500 and S&P Retailing Group, assuming a $100 investment at March 2, 2012. By fiscal 2017: BBY $211.63, S&P 500 $185.27, S&P Retailing Group $261.85.
- Selected financial data (five-year highlights):
  - Fiscal 2017 revenue $39.4 billion (stable vs. prior years); operating income $1.854 billion; net earnings from continuing operations $1.207 billion; GAAP EPS from continuing operations $3.74; total GAAP EPS $3.81; cash dividends per share $1.57. Stock price high/low in 2017: $49.40/$26.10.
  - Operating metrics (2017): comparable sales +0.3%; gross profit rate 24.0%; SG&A rate 19.2%; operating income rate 4.7%.
  - Year-end balance sheet (2017): current ratio 1.5; total assets $13.9 billion; debt $1.37 billion; total equity $4.71 billion.
  - Footprint: total stores 1,575 (1,363 domestic; 212 international); total retail square footage ~45.3 million, reflecting a multi-year decline in store count and space.
  - Notable 2017 item: $161 million (pre-tax) from CRT and LCD litigation settlements (about $100 million after tax) included in results.

top5_chunks.title: Exhibits, Financial Statement Schedules.
top5_chunks.summary:
- Part IV, Item 15 lists documents filed with Best Buy Co., Inc.’s fiscal 2017 Form 10-K (filed March 24, 2017): (1) the financial statements included in Item 8; (2) Supplementary Financial Statement Schedule II — Valuation and Qualifying Accounts; and (3) a comprehensive exhibits index.
- The exhibits index identifies key corporate and financing documents, many incorporated by reference, including: Amended and Restated Articles of Incorporation and By-Laws; indentures and supplemental indentures (2011, 2013); a Five-Year Credit Agreement (2016); and numerous equity compensation and director award agreements and plans (2004–2016), including U.S. and non-U.S. director RSU forms and a deferred compensation plan. Items marked with an asterisk denote management or compensatory plans required by Item 15(b) of Form 10-K.
- Additional exhibits include: Statements re: Computation of Ratios (12.1); Subsidiaries of the Registrant (21.1); Auditor consent from Deloitte & Touche LLP (23.1); CEO/CFO certifications under SOX Section 302 (31.1, 31.2) and Section 906/18 U.S.C. 1350 (32.1, 32.2).
- XBRL data (Exhibit 101) provides the consolidated balance sheets (as of January 28, 2017 and January 30, 2016), statements of earnings, comprehensive income, cash flows, changes in shareholders’ equity for fiscal years ended January 28, 2017; January 30, 2016; and January 31, 2015; and the related notes.
- Other schedules are omitted as not applicable or because the information appears elsewhere in the report.
- Pursuant to Regulation S-K Item 601(b)(4)(iii), certain long-term debt instruments under which the amount of securities authorized does not exceed 10% of total assets are not filed but will be furnished to the SEC upon request.
- The report clarifies that filed agreements are provided to disclose their terms and should not be relied upon for broader factual information; representations and warranties were made in their specific contexts.
- Item 16 (Form 10-K Summary): None.
- Signatures: The report is signed on behalf of the registrant by Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Hubert Joly on March 24, 2017, with additional signatures from other officers and directors.

top5_chunks.title: Business.
top5_chunks.summary:
- Company overview: Best Buy Co., Inc., incorporated in Minnesota in 1966, is a leading omni-channel retailer of technology products, services, and solutions operating in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico through stores, websites, mobile apps, and Geek Squad.
- Segments and brands: Two reportable segments—Domestic (U.S.) and International (Canada, Mexico)—operating under brands including Best Buy, bestbuy.com, Best Buy Mobile, Geek Squad, Magnolia, Pacific Sales, and others. In 2015, Canadian Future Shop operations were consolidated into the Best Buy brand, with significant store closures and conversions.
- Operations model: Centralized management of merchandising, pricing, procurement, supply chain, digital operations, marketing, and support functions; standardized store procedures with local flexibility; international operations similar to domestic.
- Offerings: Six revenue categories—Consumer Electronics; Computing and Mobile Phones; Entertainment; Appliances; Services (consultation, installation, protection, repair, tech support, etc.); and Other (sundries).
- Distribution: U.S. e-commerce fulfilled via store pickup, ship-from-store, and distribution centers; similar model in Canada and Mexico.
- Suppliers and inventory: Highly concentrated supplier base (top 20 account for ~77% of purchases; Apple, Samsung, Sony, HP, LG ~53%); generally no long-term vendor contracts; robust inventory management and vendor agreements; global sourcing for exclusive brands.
- Store footprint and strategy: ~1,200 large-format and ~400 small-format stores at FY2017 end; stores central to omni-channel strategy (ship-from-store, buy online/pick up in store); vendor shop-in-shops; ongoing space optimization and lease actions; Canadian brand consolidation reiterated.
- Intellectual property: Portfolio of trademarks and patents (e.g., Best Buy, Geek Squad, Insignia, Magnolia, My Best Buy, Yellow Tag logo) viewed as important marketing assets.
- Seasonality and working capital: Peak revenue and earnings in fiscal Q4 (holiday season); operations funded by cash, investments, operating cash flow, and revolving credit; seasonal inventory build before holidays.
- Competition: Intense competition from multi-channel retailers, e-commerce players, service providers, traditional retailers, vendors, and carriers; price transparency, sales tax dynamics, delivery speed/cost expectations, and price-matching pressure margins; scale and service used as differentiators.
- Environmental commitments: Focus on reducing operational carbon emissions (45% reduction goal by 2020 vs. 2009 baseline) and promoting energy-efficient solutions; further details in Corporate Responsibility & Sustainability Report.
- Workforce: Approximately 125,000 employees across geographies, with competitive, locally appropriate benefits and generally good employee relations.
- Public disclosures and governance: SEC reporting and filings accessible via Best Buy’s investor website and SEC channels; governance documents (bylaws, code of ethics, committee charters) available online.
- Key risk factors highlighted: Revenue and margin pressure from strong competition, online shift and delivery expectations, price transparency, higher service-driven cost structure, and rapid technological change/product life cycles affecting demand.

Item 1.  Business.
Unless the context otherwise r
equires, the use of the terms "we," "us" and "our" in this Annual Report on Form 10-K refers to Best Buy Co., Inc. and, as applicable,its consolidated subsidiar
ies. Any references to our website addresses do not constitute incorporation by reference of the information contained on the websites.Description of Business
We were incorporated in 
the state of Minnesota in 1966. Today, we are a leading provider of technology products, services and solutions. We offer these productsand services to customers who vis
it our stores, engage with Geek Squad agents or use our websites or mobile applications. We have operations in the U.S., Canadaand Mexico.
Information About Our Segments and Geographic Areas
We have two reportable seg
ments: Domestic and International. The Domestic segment is comprised of the operations in all states, districts and territories of theU.S., under various brand names including Bes
t Buy, bestbuy.com, Best Buy Mobile, Best Buy Direct, Best Buy Express, Geek Squad, Magnolia Home Theaterand Pacific Kitchen and Home.
The International segm
ent is comprised of all operations in Canada and Mexico under the brand names Best Buy, bestbuy.com.ca, bestbuy.com.mx, Best BuyExpress, Best Buy Mobile and Geek Squad.
In March 2015, we decided to consolid
ate Future Shop and Best Buy stores and websites in Canada under the Best Buy brand. This resulted in permanently closing66 Future Shop stores and converting 65 Future Shop sto
res to the Best Buy brand. Additional information on these changes is included in Item 7, Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and R
esults of Operations , and Note 4,  Restructuring Charges , of the Notes to Consolidated Financi alStatements, included in I
tem 8, Financial Statements and Supplementary Data , of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Financial information 
about our segments and geographic areas is included in Item 7, Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financia l Condition and Resultsof Operations 
, and Note 11,  Segment and Geographic Information , of the Notes to Consolidated Financi al Statements, included in Item 8, Financial Statements and Supplementary Data 
, of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Operations
Our Domestic and Internation
al segments are managed by leadership teams responsible for all areas of the business. Both segments operate an omni-channelplatform that provides 
customers the ability to shop when and where they want.Domestic Segment
Development of merchandis
e and services offerings, pricing and promotions, procurement and supply chain, online and mobile application operations, marketingand advertising and la
bor deployment across all channels are centrally managed at our corporate headquarters. In addition, support capabilities (for example,human resources, finance
 and real estate management) are generally performed at our corporate headquarters. We also have field operations that support retailteams from our corpora
te headquarters and regional locations. Our retail stores have procedures for inventory management, asset protection, transactionprocessing, customer rel
ations, store administration, product sales and services, staff training and merchandise display that are largely standardized within eachstore brand. All stores within e
ach store brand generally operate under standard procedures with a degree of flexibility for store management to address certainlocal market characteristics.
International Segment
Our Canada and Mexico store opera
tions are similar to those in our Domestic segment.Merchandise and Services
Our Domestic and Internation
al segments have offerings in six revenue categories: Consumer Electronics, Computing and Mobile Phones, Entertainment,Appliances, Services and Other. The k
ey components of each revenue category are as follows:4

Consumer Electronics - home theater, home au tomation, digital imaging, health and fitness and portable audio;•
Computing and Mobile Phones - computing and periphera ls, networking, tablets, mobile phones (including related mobile network carriercommissions), wearables (
including smart watches) and e-readers;•
Entertainment - gaming hardware and softwar e, movies, music, technology toys and other software;•
Appliances - major appliances ( for example, refrigeration, dishwashers, ovens, laundry, etc.) and small appliances (for example, coffee makers, blenders,etc.);
•
Services - consultation, design, delivery, installation, set-up, protection plans, repair, technical support and educational classes; and•
Other - snacks, beverages and other sundry items.Distribution
Domestic Segment
U.S. Best Buy online merchandise sales a
re typically either picked up at U.S. Best Buy stores or delivered directly to customers from a distribution center or retailstore. The ship-from-stor
e capability allows us to improve product availability and delivery times for customers. Most merchandise is shipped directly frommanufacturers to our dis
tribution centers located throughout the U.S. In order to meet release dates for certain products, merchandise may be shipped directly toour stores from suppliers.
International Segment
Our Canada and Mexico distribution 
model is similar to our Domestic segment model.Suppliers and Inventory
Our Domestic and Internation
al segments purchase merchandise from a variety of suppliers. In fiscal 2017, our 20 largest suppliers accounted for approximately77% of the merchandise we pur
chased, with five suppliers – Apple, Samsung, Sony, Hewlett-Packard, and LG Electronics – representing approximately 53% oftotal merchandise pur
chased. We generally do not have long-term written contracts with our vendors that would require them to continue supplying us withmerchandise or secure 
any of the key terms of our arrangements.We carefully monito
r and manage our inventory levels in an effort to match quantities on hand with consumer demand as closely as possible. Key elements to ourinventory management pro
cess include the following: continuous monitoring of historical and projected consumer demand, continuous monitoring and adjustmentof inventory receipt l
evels, agreements with vendors relating to reimbursement for the cost of markdowns or sales incentives and agreements with vendors relatingto return privileges fo
r certain products.We also have a global sourc
ing operation to design, develop, test and contract-manufacture our exclusive brand products.Store Development
We had approximately 1,200 l
arge-format and 400 small-format stores at the end of fiscal 2017 throughout our Domestic and International segments. Our storesare a vital component o
f our omni-channel strategy and represent an important competitive advantage. In the U.S., we have the ability to ship from all of our BestBuy stores. Customers may also ele
ct to pick up orders initiated online in any of our stores. In recent years, we have opened vendor store-within-a-store concepts toallow closer vendor partne
rship and a better quality customer experience. In fiscal 2018 and beyond, we will continue to look for opportunities to optimize ourstore space, renegotia
ting leases and selectively opening or closing locations to support our operations.In March 2015, we made a decision 
to consolidate Future Shop and Best Buy stores and websites in Canada under the Best Buy brand. This resulted inpermanently closing 66 Future Shop sto
res and converting 65 Future Shop stores to the Best Buy brand.Refer to Item 7, 
Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financia l Condition and Results of Operations, for tables reconciling our  Domestic and Internationalsegment stores open at the 
end of each of the last three fiscal years.5
Table of ContentsIntellectual Property
We own or have the right to use va
luable intellectual property such as trademarks, service marks and tradenames, including, but not limited to, Best Buy, Best Buy Mobile, Dynex, Geek Squad, Insignia, Magno
lia, Modal, My Best Buy, Pacific Sales, Rocketfish ,  Platinum and our Yellow Tag logo. We have secured domesti
c and international trademark and service mark registrations for many of our brands. We have also secured patents for many of ourinventions. We believe our 
intellectual property has significant value and is an important factor in the marketing of our company, our stores, our products and ourwebsites.
Seasonality
Our business, like that of many r
etailers, is seasonal. A higher proportion of our revenue and earnings is generated in the fiscal fourth quarter, which includes themajority of the holiday shopp
ing season in the U.S., Canada and Mexico.Working Capital
We fund our business operations th
rough a combination of available cash and cash equivalents, short-term investments and cash flows generated from operations.In addition, our revolving cr
edit facilities are available for additional working capital needs, for general corporate purposes and investment and growthopportunities. Our working capita
l needs typically increase in the months leading up to the holiday shopping season as we purchase inventory in advance ofexpected sales.
Competition
Our competitors are primarily
 multi-channel retailers, internet-based businesses, technology service providers, traditional store-based retailers and vendors andmobile network carrie
rs, who offer their products and services directly to customers. We believe our ability to deliver a high quality customer experience offers usa key competitive advan
tage. Some of our competitors have low cost operating structures and seek to compete for sales primarily on price. In addition, in the U.S.,online-only operators are
 exempt from collecting sales taxes in certain states. We believe this advantage will continue to be eroded as sales tax rules are re-evaluated at both the st
ate and federal levels. We carefully monitor pricing offered by other retailers, and maintaining price competitiveness is one of our ongoingpriorities. In addition, we h
ave a price-matching policy in the U.S. that allows customers to request that we match a price offered by certain retail store and onlineoperators. In order to al
low this, we are focused on maintaining efficient operations and leveraging the economies of scale available to us through our globalvendor partnerships. We bel
ieve our dedicated and knowledgeable people, integrated online and retail assets, broad product assortment, strong vendorrelationships, range of fo
cused service and support offerings, distinct store formats, brand marketing strategies and supply chain are important ways in which wemaintain this advantage.
Environmental Matters
Best Buy is committe
d to positively impacting the environment and our communities. We believe that effectively managing our environmental impacts, settingsustainability goals and adv
ancing energy-efficient consumer solutions create long-term value for all of our stakeholders.  
We are continuously looking fo
r cost-effective solutions to minimize carbon emissions in our operations. In fiscal year 2016, we set a new goal to reduce our owncarbon emissions by 45 percent by 2020 
(over a 2009 baseline), from both operational reductions and renewable sourcing. 
See our Best Buy Corporate Responsibility & Sust
ainability Report for further information on environmental performance.Number of Employees
At the end of fiscal 2017, we employ
ed approximately 125,000  full-time, part-time and seasonal employees in the U.S., Canada, Mexico and our sourcing office inChina. We consider our employe
e relations to be good. We offer our employees a wide array of company-paid benefits that vary within our company due tocustomary local practices and
 statutory requirements, which we believe are competitive locally and in the aggregate relative to others in our industry.6

top1_chunks.title: Selected Financial Data.
top1_chunks.summary:
This partial document is Item 6: Selected Financial Data from Best Buy Co., Inc.’s Form 10-K, presenting five-year financial highlights (FY2015–FY2019) to be read with MD&A (Item 7) and the audited financial statements (Item 8).

Key contents and highlights:
- Consolidated results (in millions): Revenue rose from $40.3B (2015) to $42.9B (2019); operating income hovered around $1.4B–$1.9B, reaching $1.9B in 2019; net earnings from continuing operations increased to $1.464B in 2019 (from $999M in 2018). Discontinued operations had minimal impact in recent years.
- Per-share data: EPS from continuing operations was $5.20 in 2019 (vs. $3.26 in 2018); total EPS matched $5.20 in 2019; cash dividends per share increased to $1.80 in 2019.
- Operating metrics: Comparable sales growth was 4.8% in 2019 (5.6% in 2018); gross profit rate at 23.2% (down from 24.0% in 2017); SG&A rate at 18.7%; operating income rate steady at 4.4% in 2019.
- Year-end financial position: Current ratio 1.2 (2019); total assets $12.9B; debt $1.39B; total equity $3.31B.
- Store footprint: Continued rationalization—domestic stores declined to 1,026 and international to 212 (total 1,238 in 2019); total retail square footage decreased to 44.1M from 48.2M in 2015.
- Notable footnotes/adjustments (2019): Includes $46M restructuring charges ($35M net of tax); $35M in GreatCall acquisition-related costs including intangible amortization ($28M net); $7M one-time employee bonus tied to U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act ($5M net); and $25M of subsequent Tax Act adjustments. Fiscal 2018 included a 53rd week; all other years had 52 weeks.

- Market and dividends: Best Buy’s common stock trades on the NYSE under “BBY.” The company has paid regular quarterly cash dividends since fiscal 2004, issued special dividends in Q1 fiscal 2016 and 2017, and on February 28, 2019 increased the regular quarterly dividend from $0.45 to $0.50 per share. Future dividends depend on earnings, capital needs, financial condition, and other factors.
- Holders: As of March 26, 2019, there were 267,804,388 holders of record of the company’s common stock.
- Share repurchases: On February 23, 2019, the Board authorized a new $3.0 billion share repurchase program, superseding the February 2017 $5.0 billion authorization (with $1.5 billion remaining as of February 2, 2019). In fiscal 2019, the company repurchased and retired 21.2 million shares for $1.5 billion; from fiscal year-end to March 26, 2019, it repurchased an additional 0.9 million shares for $62 million. In Q4 fiscal 2019, 5.8 million shares were repurchased at an average price of $60.12, with $1.536 billion remaining under the 2017 program at quarter-end; a footnote notes $1.9 billion was available at the start of Q4 and $349 million was used during the quarter.
- Stock performance graph: Presents five-year cumulative total shareholder return versus the S&P 500 and S&P Retailing Group, assuming $100 invested at the end of fiscal 2014. As of February 2, 2019: Best Buy $290.98; S&P 500 $168.19; S&P Retailing Group $256.26. Includes a standard disclaimer that the graph is not soliciting material nor deemed filed.
- Selected financial data (five-year highlights):
  - Revenue: $42.9B (2019), $42.2B (2018), $39.4B (2017), $39.5B (2016), $40.3B (2015).
  - Operating income around $1.9B in 2019 and 2018.
  - Net earnings from continuing operations: $1.464B (2019), $0.999B (2018), $1.207B (2017), $0.807B (2016), $1.246B (2015).
  - EPS from continuing operations: $5.20 (2019), $3.26 (2018), $3.74 (2017), $2.30 (2016), $3.53 (2015). Cash dividends declared and paid per share: $1.80 (2019), $1.36 (2018), $1.57 (2017), $1.43 (2016), $0.72 (2015).
  - Operating stats: Comparable sales growth 4.8% (2019) and 5.6% (2018); gross profit rate 23.2% (2019); SG&A rate 18.7% (2019); operating income rate 4.4% (2019).
  - Year-end: Current ratio 1.2 (2019); total assets $12.9B; debt $1.388B; equity $3.306B. Store count declined over time: Domestic 1,026 and International 212 (total 1,238) in 2019; total retail square footage 44.1M.
  - Footnotes: Fiscal 2019 includes restructuring charges ($46M pre-tax), GreatCall acquisition-related charges and amortization ($35M pre-tax), and a one-time bonus related to U.S. tax reform ($7M pre-tax), plus $25M of subsequent Tax Act adjustments. Fiscal 2018 included 53 weeks.

top5_chunks.title: Selected Financial Data.
top5_chunks.summary:
- Presents Best Buy’s Item 6 Selected Financial Data with five-year financial highlights (2015–2019), including revenue, operating income, net earnings (including/discontinued operations), EPS, dividends, comparable sales growth, gross margin, SG&A rate, operating margin, current ratio, total assets, debt, equity, store counts by segment, and retail square footage.
- Notes key one-time or non-recurring items affecting results:
  - 2019: Restructuring charges; GreatCall acquisition-related costs and intangible amortization; one-time employee bonus tied to U.S. tax reform; Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA) subsequent adjustments.
  - 2018 (53-week year): One-time employee bonus and Best Buy Foundation contribution tied to TCJA; significant TCJA charges.
  - 2017: Net benefit from CRT/LCD litigation settlements (net of fees).
  - 2016: Restructuring charges.
  - 2015: Discrete tax benefit from reorganizing European legal entities.
- Details methodology for comparable sales:
  - Includes stores, websites, and call centers open at least 14 months; exclusions for relocations/remodels; timing for acquisitions entering comp base.
  - Explains Canadian brand consolidation impacts (temporary removal of International comps through Q3 FY2017; reinstated in Q4 FY2017).
  - Excludes FY2018’s extra week from comps.
  - Excludes revenue from U.S. Best Buy Mobile stand-alone stores beginning March 2018 (due to planned closures).
  - Excludes GreatCall from FY2019 comps per acquisition policy.
- Clarifies definitions: current ratio calculation; store counts include Outlet Centers.
- Introduces Item 7 MD&A structure: Overview, Business Strategy, Results of Operations, Liquidity and Capital Resources, Critical Accounting Estimates, New Accounting Pronouncements.
- Company overview highlights:
  - Mission to enrich consumers’ lives through technology across entertainment, productivity, communication, food prep, security, and health/wellness.
  - Operations in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico; two reportable segments (Domestic, which includes GreatCall, and International).
  - Fiscal year ends on the Saturday nearest end of January; FY2018 had 53 weeks, FY2019 and FY2017 had 52 weeks.

top1_chunks.title: Selected Financial Data.
top1_chunks.summary:
- Section covered: Item 6, Selected Financial Data from Best Buy’s Form 10-K, presenting five-year financial highlights (2013–2017; 2016 is an 11‑month fiscal year) to be read with MD&A (Item 7) and Financial Statements (Item 8).
- Income statement highlights: Revenue remained relatively stable around $39–41 billion; operating income improved to $1.85 billion in 2017 (operating margin 4.7% vs. 3.5% in 2016); net earnings from continuing operations rose to $1.21 billion in 2017 after weaker prior years (2013 showed a loss).
- Discontinued operations: Small gains/losses across the period; total net earnings attributable to shareholders reached $1.23 billion in 2017.
- Per-share data: EPS from continuing operations increased to $3.74 in 2017; total diluted EPS reached $3.81; cash dividends rose steadily (from $0.66 in 2013 to $1.57 in 2017); stock price range expanded (2017 high $49.40, low $26.10).
- Operating metrics: Comparable sales modestly positive in 2015–2017 (0.3–0.5%) after declines in 2013–2014; gross profit rate improved to 24.0% in 2017; SG&A rate around 19–20%; operating margin strengthened.
- Balance sheet and liquidity: Current ratio near 1.4–1.5; total assets about $13.9 billion in 2017; debt declined from $2.29 billion (2013) to $1.37 billion (2017); total equity $4.71 billion in 2017.
- Footprint: Continued rationalization of stores and space—total stores fell from 1,779 (2013–2014) to 1,575 (2017), with notable reduction internationally; retail square footage declined correspondingly.
- Notable item: 2017 results include $161 million ($100 million net of tax) from CRT and LCD litigation settlements, affecting net earnings; referenced to Note 12, Contingencies and Commitments.

- Covers Item 5 (Market for Registrant’s Common Equity, Related Stockholder Matters and Issuer Purchases of Equity Securities) and Item 6 (Selected Financial Data) in Part II of a Form 10-K for Best Buy (ticker: BBY, NYSE).
- Dividends: Regular quarterly cash dividend initiated in 2004 and paid every quarter since; special dividends paid in early fiscal 2016 and fiscal 2017; on March 1, 2017, the regular quarterly dividend was increased 21% to $0.34 per share. Dividend policy remains subject to earnings, capital needs, and other factors. Quarter-by-quarter stock price highs/lows and dividends for fiscal 2016–2017 are provided.
- Stockholders: 2,566 holders of record as of March 20, 2017.
- Share repurchases: Original $5.0 billion authorization from June 2011 (no expiration). In fiscal 2017, 21.1 million shares were repurchased and retired for $0.8 billion; $2.2 billion remained available at year-end. In February 2017, a new $5.0 billion authorization superseded the 2011 plan; on March 1, 2017, the company announced intent to repurchase $3 billion over the next two years. Detailed Q4 fiscal 2017 activity: 5.14 million shares repurchased at an average $43.35; authorization remaining declined from $2.5 billion to $2.238 billion.
- Comparative performance: A five-year cumulative total shareholder return graph (not deemed soliciting or “filed” material) compares BBY to the S&P 500 and S&P Retailing Group, assuming a $100 investment at March 2, 2012. By fiscal 2017: BBY $211.63, S&P 500 $185.27, S&P Retailing Group $261.85.
- Selected financial data (five-year highlights):
  - Fiscal 2017 revenue $39.4 billion (stable vs. prior years); operating income $1.854 billion; net earnings from continuing operations $1.207 billion; GAAP EPS from continuing operations $3.74; total GAAP EPS $3.81; cash dividends per share $1.57. Stock price high/low in 2017: $49.40/$26.10.
  - Operating metrics (2017): comparable sales +0.3%; gross profit rate 24.0%; SG&A rate 19.2%; operating income rate 4.7%.
  - Year-end balance sheet (2017): current ratio 1.5; total assets $13.9 billion; debt $1.37 billion; total equity $4.71 billion.
  - Footprint: total stores 1,575 (1,363 domestic; 212 international); total retail square footage ~45.3 million, reflecting a multi-year decline in store count and space.
  - Notable 2017 item: $161 million (pre-tax) from CRT and LCD litigation settlements (about $100 million after tax) included in results.

top5_chunks.title: Business.
top5_chunks.summary:
- Company overview: Best Buy Co., Inc., incorporated in Minnesota in 1966, is a leading omni-channel retailer of technology products, services, and solutions operating in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico through stores, websites, mobile apps, and Geek Squad.
- Segments and brands: Two reportable segments—Domestic (U.S.) and International (Canada, Mexico)—operating under brands including Best Buy, bestbuy.com, Best Buy Mobile, Geek Squad, Magnolia, Pacific Sales, and others. In 2015, Canadian Future Shop operations were consolidated into the Best Buy brand, with significant store closures and conversions.
- Operations model: Centralized management of merchandising, pricing, procurement, supply chain, digital operations, marketing, and support functions; standardized store procedures with local flexibility; international operations similar to domestic.
- Offerings: Six revenue categories—Consumer Electronics; Computing and Mobile Phones; Entertainment; Appliances; Services (consultation, installation, protection, repair, tech support, etc.); and Other (sundries).
- Distribution: U.S. e-commerce fulfilled via store pickup, ship-from-store, and distribution centers; similar model in Canada and Mexico.
- Suppliers and inventory: Highly concentrated supplier base (top 20 account for ~77% of purchases; Apple, Samsung, Sony, HP, LG ~53%); generally no long-term vendor contracts; robust inventory management and vendor agreements; global sourcing for exclusive brands.
- Store footprint and strategy: ~1,200 large-format and ~400 small-format stores at FY2017 end; stores central to omni-channel strategy (ship-from-store, buy online/pick up in store); vendor shop-in-shops; ongoing space optimization and lease actions; Canadian brand consolidation reiterated.
- Intellectual property: Portfolio of trademarks and patents (e.g., Best Buy, Geek Squad, Insignia, Magnolia, My Best Buy, Yellow Tag logo) viewed as important marketing assets.
- Seasonality and working capital: Peak revenue and earnings in fiscal Q4 (holiday season); operations funded by cash, investments, operating cash flow, and revolving credit; seasonal inventory build before holidays.
- Competition: Intense competition from multi-channel retailers, e-commerce players, service providers, traditional retailers, vendors, and carriers; price transparency, sales tax dynamics, delivery speed/cost expectations, and price-matching pressure margins; scale and service used as differentiators.
- Environmental commitments: Focus on reducing operational carbon emissions (45% reduction goal by 2020 vs. 2009 baseline) and promoting energy-efficient solutions; further details in Corporate Responsibility & Sustainability Report.
- Workforce: Approximately 125,000 employees across geographies, with competitive, locally appropriate benefits and generally good employee relations.
- Public disclosures and governance: SEC reporting and filings accessible via Best Buy’s investor website and SEC channels; governance documents (bylaws, code of ethics, committee charters) available online.
- Key risk factors highlighted: Revenue and margin pressure from strong competition, online shift and delivery expectations, price transparency, higher service-driven cost structure, and rapid technological change/product life cycles affecting demand.

Item 1.  Business.
Unless the context otherwise r
equires, the use of the terms "we," "us" and "our" in this Annual Report on Form 10-K refers to Best Buy Co., Inc. and, as applicable,its consolidated subsidiar
ies. Any references to our website addresses do not constitute incorporation by reference of the information contained on the websites.Description of Business
We were incorporated in 
the state of Minnesota in 1966. Today, we are a leading provider of technology products, services and solutions. We offer these productsand services to customers who vis
it our stores, engage with Geek Squad agents or use our websites or mobile applications. We have operations in the U.S., Canadaand Mexico.
Information About Our Segments and Geographic Areas
We have two reportable seg
ments: Domestic and International. The Domestic segment is comprised of the operations in all states, districts and territories of theU.S., under various brand names including Bes
t Buy, bestbuy.com, Best Buy Mobile, Best Buy Direct, Best Buy Express, Geek Squad, Magnolia Home Theaterand Pacific Kitchen and Home.
The International segm
ent is comprised of all operations in Canada and Mexico under the brand names Best Buy, bestbuy.com.ca, bestbuy.com.mx, Best BuyExpress, Best Buy Mobile and Geek Squad.
In March 2015, we decided to consolid
ate Future Shop and Best Buy stores and websites in Canada under the Best Buy brand. This resulted in permanently closing66 Future Shop stores and converting 65 Future Shop sto
res to the Best Buy brand. Additional information on these changes is included in Item 7, Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and R
esults of Operations , and Note 4,  Restructuring Charges , of the Notes to Consolidated Financi alStatements, included in I
tem 8, Financial Statements and Supplementary Data , of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Financial information 
about our segments and geographic areas is included in Item 7, Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financia l Condition and Resultsof Operations 
, and Note 11,  Segment and Geographic Information , of the Notes to Consolidated Financi al Statements, included in Item 8, Financial Statements and Supplementary Data 
, of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Operations
Our Domestic and Internation
al segments are managed by leadership teams responsible for all areas of the business. Both segments operate an omni-channelplatform that provides 
customers the ability to shop when and where they want.Domestic Segment
Development of merchandis
e and services offerings, pricing and promotions, procurement and supply chain, online and mobile application operations, marketingand advertising and la
bor deployment across all channels are centrally managed at our corporate headquarters. In addition, support capabilities (for example,human resources, finance
 and real estate management) are generally performed at our corporate headquarters. We also have field operations that support retailteams from our corpora
te headquarters and regional locations. Our retail stores have procedures for inventory management, asset protection, transactionprocessing, customer rel
ations, store administration, product sales and services, staff training and merchandise display that are largely standardized within eachstore brand. All stores within e
ach store brand generally operate under standard procedures with a degree of flexibility for store management to address certainlocal market characteristics.
International Segment
Our Canada and Mexico store opera
tions are similar to those in our Domestic segment.Merchandise and Services
Our Domestic and Internation
al segments have offerings in six revenue categories: Consumer Electronics, Computing and Mobile Phones, Entertainment,Appliances, Services and Other. The k
ey components of each revenue category are as follows:4
Table of Contents•
Consumer Electronics - home theater, home au tomation, digital imaging, health and fitness and portable audio;•
Computing and Mobile Phones - computing and periphera ls, networking, tablets, mobile phones (including related mobile network carriercommissions), wearables (
including smart watches) and e-readers;•
Entertainment - gaming hardware and softwar e, movies, music, technology toys and other software;•
Appliances - major appliances ( for example, refrigeration, dishwashers, ovens, laundry, etc.) and small appliances (for example, coffee makers, blenders,etc.);
•
Services - consultation, design, delivery, installation, set-up, protection plans, repair, technical support and educational classes; and•
Other - snacks, beverages and other sundry items.Distribution
Domestic Segment
U.S. Best Buy online merchandise sales a
re typically either picked up at U.S. Best Buy stores or delivered directly to customers from a distribution center or retailstore. The ship-from-stor
e capability allows us to improve product availability and delivery times for customers. Most merchandise is shipped directly frommanufacturers to our dis
tribution centers located throughout the U.S. In order to meet release dates for certain products, merchandise may be shipped directly toour stores from suppliers.
International Segment
Our Canada and Mexico distribution 
model is similar to our Domestic segment model.Suppliers and Inventory
Our Domestic and Internation
al segments purchase merchandise from a variety of suppliers. In fiscal 2017, our 20 largest suppliers accounted for approximately77% of the merchandise we pur
chased, with five suppliers – Apple, Samsung, Sony, Hewlett-Packard, and LG Electronics – representing approximately 53% oftotal merchandise pur
chased. We generally do not have long-term written contracts with our vendors that would require them to continue supplying us withmerchandise or secure 
any of the key terms of our arrangements.We carefully monito
r and manage our inventory levels in an effort to match quantities on hand with consumer demand as closely as possible. Key elements to ourinventory management pro
cess include the following: continuous monitoring of historical and projected consumer demand, continuous monitoring and adjustmentof inventory receipt l
evels, agreements with vendors relating to reimbursement for the cost of markdowns or sales incentives and agreements with vendors relatingto return privileges fo
r certain products.We also have a global sourc
ing operation to design, develop, test and contract-manufacture our exclusive brand products.Store Development
We had approximately 1,200 l
arge-format and 400 small-format stores at the end of fiscal 2017 throughout our Domestic and International segments. Our storesare a vital component o
f our omni-channel strategy and represent an important competitive advantage. In the U.S., we have the ability to ship from all of our BestBuy stores. Customers may also ele
ct to pick up orders initiated online in any of our stores. In recent years, we have opened vendor store-within-a-store concepts toallow closer vendor partne
rship and a better quality customer experience. In fiscal 2018 and beyond, we will continue to look for opportunities to optimize ourstore space, renegotia
ting leases and selectively opening or closing locations to support our operations.In March 2015, we made a decision 
to consolidate Future Shop and Best Buy stores and websites in Canada under the Best Buy brand. This resulted inpermanently closing 66 Future Shop sto
res and converting 65 Future Shop stores to the Best Buy brand.Refer to Item 7, 
Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financia l Condition and Results of Operations, for tables reconciling our  Domestic and Internationalsegment stores open at the 
end of each of the last three fiscal years.5
Table of ContentsIntellectual Property
We own or have the right to use va
luable intellectual property such as trademarks, service marks and tradenames, including, but not limited to, Best Buy, Best Buy Mobile, Dynex, Geek Squad, Insignia, Magno
lia, Modal, My Best Buy, Pacific Sales, Rocketfish ,  Platinum and our Yellow Tag logo. We have secured domesti
c and international trademark and service mark registrations for many of our brands. We have also secured patents for many of ourinventions. We believe our 
intellectual property has significant value and is an important factor in the marketing of our company, our stores, our products and ourwebsites.
Seasonality
Our business, like that of many r
etailers, is seasonal. A higher proportion of our revenue and earnings is generated in the fiscal fourth quarter, which includes themajority of the holiday shopp
ing season in the U.S., Canada and Mexico.Working Capital
We fund our business operations th
rough a combination of available cash and cash equivalents, short-term investments and cash flows generated from operations.In addition, our revolving cr
edit facilities are available for additional working capital needs, for general corporate purposes and investment and growthopportunities. Our working capita
l needs typically increase in the months leading up to the holiday shopping season as we purchase inventory in advance ofexpected sales.
Competition
Our competitors are primarily
 multi-channel retailers, internet-based businesses, technology service providers, traditional store-based retailers and vendors andmobile network carrie
rs, who offer their products and services directly to customers. We believe our ability to deliver a high quality customer experience offers usa key competitive advan
tage. Some of our competitors have low cost operating structures and seek to compete for sales primarily on price. In addition, in the U.S.,online-only operators are
 exempt from collecting sales taxes in certain states. We believe this advantage will continue to be eroded as sales tax rules are re-evaluated at both the st
ate and federal levels. We carefully monitor pricing offered by other retailers, and maintaining price competitiveness is one of our ongoingpriorities. In addition, we h
ave a price-matching policy in the U.S. that allows customers to request that we match a price offered by certain retail store and onlineoperators. In order to al
low this, we are focused on maintaining efficient operations and leveraging the economies of scale available to us through our globalvendor partnerships. We bel
ieve our dedicated and knowledgeable people, integrated online and retail assets, broad product assortment, strong vendorrelationships, range of fo
cused service and support offerings, distinct store formats, brand marketing strategies and supply chain are important ways in which wemaintain this advantage.
Environmental Matters
Best Buy is committe
d to positively impacting the environment and our communities. We believe that effectively managing our environmental impacts, settingsustainability goals and adv
ancing energy-efficient consumer solutions create long-term value for all of our stakeholders.  
We are continuously looking fo
r cost-effective solutions to minimize carbon emissions in our operations. In fiscal year 2016, we set a new goal to reduce our owncarbon emissions by 45 percent by 2020 
(over a 2009 baseline), from both operational reductions and renewable sourcing. 
See our Best Buy Corporate Responsibility & Sust
ainability Report for further information on environmental performance.Number of Employees
At the end of fiscal 2017, we employ
ed approximately 125,000  full-time, part-time and seasonal employees in the U.S., Canada, Mexico and our sourcing office inChina. We consider our employe
e relations to be good. We offer our employees a wide array of company-paid benefits that vary within our company due tocustomary local practices and
 statutory requirements, which we believe are competitive locally and in the aggregate relative to others in our industry.6

- SEC Form 10-K filing for Best Buy Co., Inc. (Commission file 1-9595), a Minnesota corporation headquartered in Richfield, MN; common stock listed on NYSE.
- Registrant status and compliance: well-known seasoned issuer; large accelerated filer; not a shell company; compliant with reporting and interactive data filing requirements; delinquent filer disclosure not contained; market value of non-affiliate equity approx. $7.8B as of July 29, 2016; 309,110,840 shares outstanding as of March 20, 2017.
- Documents incorporated by reference: portions of the 2017 Proxy Statement for Part III.
- Cautionary forward-looking statements under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, referencing Item 1A Risk Factors and noting no obligation to update.
- Table of contents outlines Parts I–IV, including Business, Risk Factors, Properties, Legal Proceedings, Market and Stockholder Matters, MD&A, Financial Statements, Controls and Procedures, Governance and Compensation items, and Exhibits.
- Business description:
  - Best Buy is a leading provider of technology products, services, and solutions across stores, online, mobile apps, and Geek Squad; operations in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico.
  - Two reportable segments: Domestic (U.S.) and International (Canada and Mexico), operating an omni-channel model.
  - Brands include Best Buy, bestbuy.com, Best Buy Mobile, Geek Squad, Magnolia Home Theater, Pacific Kitchen and Home, Best Buy Express, and regional websites.
  - Canada brand consolidation (March 2015): Future Shop integrated into Best Buy, closing 66 stores and converting 65 to Best Buy.
- Operations:
  - Centralized U.S. management for merchandising, pricing, supply chain, e-commerce, marketing, labor deployment, and corporate support; standardized store procedures with local flexibility.
  - International store operations similar to Domestic.
- Merchandise and services categories:
  - Consumer Electronics; Computing and Mobile Phones; Entertainment; Appliances; Services (consultation, installation, protection plans, repair, support, classes); and Other (snacks, beverages, sundries).
- Distribution:
  - U.S. online orders fulfilled via store pickup or delivery from distribution centers or stores; ship-from-store capability; most merchandise shipped from manufacturers to distribution centers, with direct-to-store for certain releases.
  - Canada and Mexico use a similar model.
- Suppliers and inventory:
  - In fiscal 2017, top 20 suppliers represented ~77% of purchases; Apple, Samsung, Sony, HP, and LG comprised ~53%.
  - Generally no long-term vendor contracts; inventory managed via demand monitoring, receipt adjustments, vendor markdown/return agreements; global sourcing for exclusive-brand products.
- Store development:
  - Approximately 1,200 large-format and 400 small-format stores across segments at fiscal 2017 year-end.
  - Omni-channel advantages include ship-from-store and in-store pickup; vendor store-within-a-store concepts; ongoing space optimization, lease renegotiations, and selective openings/closures.
- Intellectual property:
  - Portfolio of trademarks and patents; notable marks include Best Buy, Best Buy Mobile, Geek Squad, Magnolia, Insignia, Dynex, Rocketfish, Pacific Sales, Modal, Platinum, My Best Buy, and the Yellow Tag logo.
- Seasonality: Concentration of revenue and earnings in fiscal Q4 due to holiday shopping.
- Working capital: Funded by cash, equivalents, short-term investments, operating cash flows, and revolving credit facilities; needs increase ahead of holiday season.
- Competition: Multi-channel and online retailers, service providers, traditional retailers, vendors, and mobile carriers; focus on customer experience, price competitiveness, price matching, scale, vendor partnerships, and integrated assets; note on evolving sales tax dynamics for online operators.
- Environmental matters: Commitment to sustainability; goal to reduce carbon emissions by 45% by 2020 vs. 2009 baseline through operational efficiencies and renewable sourcing; reference to Corporate Responsibility & Sustainability Report.
- Employees: Approximately 125,000 full-time, part-time, and seasonal employees in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, and a sourcing office in China; positive employee relations and competitive benefits aligned with local practices.

top1_chunks.summary:
- SEC Form 10-K filing for Best Buy Co., Inc. (fiscal year ended January 28, 2023), including registrant information, NYSE listing (BBY), filer status (well-known seasoned issuer; large accelerated filer), Section 404(b) ICFR attestation, market value of non-affiliate equity as of July 29, 2022, and shares outstanding as of March 15, 2023.
- Indications of reporting compliance (Exchange Act filings and Interactive Data Files), and that the company is not a shell company.
- Documents incorporated by reference: portions of the 2023 Definitive Proxy Statement for Part III.
- Safe harbor cautionary statement for forward-looking statements under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995.
- Table of Contents outlining Parts I–IV, including Business, Risk Factors, MD&A, Market Risk, Financial Statements, Controls and Procedures, and other standard 10-K items.
- Item 1. Business: Company overview—incorporated in Minnesota (1966); purpose to enrich lives through technology; vision to personalize and humanize technology solutions; operations in the U.S. and Canada.
- Reportable segments: Domestic (U.S. and Best Buy Health) and International (Canada). Domestic brands and domains include Best Buy, Best Buy Ads, Best Buy Business, Best Buy Health, CST, Current Health, Geek Squad, Lively, Magnolia, Pacific Kitchen and Home, TechLiquidators, Yardbird, and related websites; International brands include Best Buy, Best Buy Mobile, Geek Squad, and bestbuy.ca. Mexico stores closed by end of Q1 FY22.
- Recent acquisitions (FY22): Current Health Ltd. and Yardbird Furniture.
- Operations model: omnichannel platform (online, in-store, in-home); centrally managed merchandising, pricing, supply chain, digital, marketing, and support functions; standardized store procedures with localized flexibility; distinct leadership and operations for Best Buy Health supported by enterprise capabilities.
- Merchandise and services organized into six revenue categories:
  1) Computing and Mobile Phones (computers, peripherals, mobile, networking, tablets, wearables),
  2) Consumer Electronics (imaging, health/fitness, home theater, portable audio, smart home),
  3) Appliances (large and small),
  4) Entertainment (drones, gaming, media, toys, VR, software),
  5) Services (consultation, delivery, design, health services, installation, memberships, repair, setup, tech support, warranties),
  6) Other (baby, food/beverage, luggage, outdoor living, sporting goods).

- Company overview: Incorporated in Minnesota in 1966; purpose is to enrich lives through technology; vision to personalize and humanize technology solutions for every stage of life; operates in the U.S. and Canada via an omnichannel model (online, in-store, in-home).
- Segments:
  - Domestic: U.S. operations plus Best Buy Health; brands include Best Buy, Best Buy Ads, Best Buy Business, Best Buy Health, CST, Current Health, Geek Squad, Lively, Magnolia, Pacific Kitchen and Home, TechLiquidators, and Yardbird; domains include bestbuy.com, currenthealth.com, lively.com, techliquidators.com, yardbird.com.
  - International: Canada operations under Best Buy, Best Buy Mobile, and Geek Squad; domain bestbuy.ca. All Mexico stores closed by end of Q1 fiscal 2022.
- Recent acquisitions (fiscal 2022): Current Health Ltd. and Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture.
- Operations and management:
  - Both segments run an omnichannel platform.
  - Centralized management of merchandising and services development, pricing/promotions, procurement and supply chain, digital/app operations, marketing/advertising, and labor deployment; corporate support functions (HR, finance, IT, real estate) at headquarters.
  - Field operations support retail, services, and in-home teams; stores use standardized procedures with local flexibility; strategic decisions (locations, formats, assortments, fulfillment) handled at market/region level.
  - Best Buy Health has dedicated leadership and operations, with support from enterprise capabilities.
- Revenue categories (six) and key components:
  - Computing & Mobile Phones: desktops, notebooks, peripherals, mobile phones (incl. carrier commissions), networking, tablets/e-readers, wearables.
  - Consumer Electronics: digital imaging, health/fitness products, home theater, portable audio (headphones/speakers), smart home.
  - Appliances: large (dishwashers, laundry, ovens, refrigerators) and small (blenders, coffee makers, vacuums).
  - Entertainment: drones, gaming (hardware, peripherals, software), movies, music, toys, virtual reality, other software.
  - Services: consultation, delivery, design, health-related services, installation, memberships, repair, setup, technical support, warranty-related services.
  - Other: baby, food & beverage, luggage, outdoor living, sporting goods.
top5_chunks.text:
Unless the context otherwise requires, the terms “we,” “us” and “our” in this Annual Report on Form 10-K refer to Best Buy Co., Inc. and, as applicable, its  
consolidated subsidiaries. Any references to our website addresses do not constitute incorporation by reference of the information contained on the websites.
 
Description of Business
 
We were incorporated in the state of Minnesota in 1966. We are driven by our purpose to enrich lives through technology and our vision to personalize and  
humanize technology solutions for every stage of life. We accomplish this by leveraging our combination of technology and a human touch to meet our  
customers’  everyday needs, whether they come to us online, visit our stores or invite us into their homes. W e have operations in the U.S. and Canada.
 
Segments and Geographic Areas
 
We have two reportable segments: Domestic and International. The Domestic segment is comprised of our operations in all states, districts and territories of the  
U.S. and our Best Buy Health business, and includes the brand names Best Buy , Best Buy Ads, Best Buy Business, Best Buy Health, CST , Current Health, Geek  
Squad, Lively , Magnolia, Pacific Kitchen and Home, TechLiquidators and Yardbird and the domain names bestbuy .com, currenthealth.com, lively .com,  
techliquidators.com and yardbird.com. All of our former stores in Mexico were closed as of the end of the first quarter of fiscal 2022, and our International  
segment is comprised of all operations in Canada under the brand names Best Buy , Best Buy Mobile and Geek Squad and the domain name bestbuy .ca.
 
In fiscal 2022, we acquired all of the outstanding shares of Current Health Ltd. (“Current Health”) and Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture (“Y ardbird”).
 
Operations
 
Our Domestic and International segments are managed by leadership teams responsible for all areas of the business. Both segments operate an omnichannel  
platform that allows customers to come to us online, visit our stores or invite us into their homes.
 
Development of merchandise and service of ferings, pricing and promotions, procurement and supply chain, online and mobile application operations, marketing  
and advertising and labor deployment across all channels are centrally managed. In addition, support capabilities (for example, human resources, finance,  
information technology and real estate management) operate from our corporate headquarters. W e also have field operations that support retail, services and in-
home teams from our corporate headquarters and regional locations. Our retail stores have procedures for inventory management, asset protection, transaction  
processing, customer relations, store administration, product sales and services, staf f training and merchandise display that are largely standardized. All stores  
generally operate under standard procedures with a degree of flexibility for store management to address certain local market characteristics. While day-to-day  
operations of our stores are led by store management, more strategic decisions regarding, for example, store locations, format, category assortment and  
fulfillment strategy are addressed at a market or regional level.
 
Our Best Buy Health business has a dedicated leadership team and operations team. The Best Buy Health leadership team manages the day-to-day af fairs of all  
aspects of its business, while receiving support from certain Best Buy enterprise capabilities.
 
Merchandise and Services
 
Our Domestic and International segments have of ferings in six revenue categories. The key components of each revenue category are as follows:
 
·Computing and Mobile Phones  - computing (including desktops, notebooks and peripherals), mobile phones (including related mobile network carrier  
commissions), networking, tablets (including e-readers) and wearables (including smartwatches);
·Consumer Electronics  - digital imaging, health and fitness products, home theater , portable audio (including headphones and portable speakers) and  
smart home;
·Appliances  - large appliances (including dishwashers, laundry , ovens and refrigerators) and small appliances (including blenders, cof fee makers and  
vacuums);
·Entertainment  - drones, gaming (including hardware, peripherals and software), movies, music, toys, virtual reality and other software;
·Services  - consultation, delivery , design, health-related services, installation, memberships, repair , set-up, technical support and warranty-related  
services; and
·Other  - other product of ferings, including baby , food and beverage, luggage, outdoor living and sporting goods.

Item 5. Market for Registrant's Common Equity , Related Stockholder Matters and Issuer Purchases of Equity Securities.
 
Market Information and Dividends
 
Our common stock is traded on the New York Stock Exchange (“NYSE”) under the ticker symbol BBY . In fiscal 2004, our Board initiated the payment of a regular  
quarterly cash dividend with respect to shares of our common stock. A quarterly cash dividend has been paid in each subsequent quarter . On March 2, 2023 , we 
announced an increase in our regular quarterly dividend from $0.88 per share to $0.92 per share. Future dividend payments will depend on our earnings, capital  
requirements, financial condition and other factors considered relevant by our Board.
 
Holders
 
As of March 15, 2023, there were 1,955 holders of record of our common stock.
 
Purchases of Equity Securities by the Issuer and Affiliated Purchasers
 
On February 28, 2022, our Board approved a $5.0 billion share repurchase authorization, which replaced the $5.0 billion share repurchase program authorized  
on February 16, 2021. There is no expiration date governing the period over which we can repurchase shares under this authorization. During fiscal 2023, we  
repurchased and retired 1 1.8 million shares at a cost of $1.0 billion. For additional information, see “Share Repurchases and Dividends” in Item 7, Management’ s 
Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations , and Note 9, Shareholders’  Equity , of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements,  
included in Item 8, Financial Statements and Supplementary Data , of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

Corie S. Barry  was appointed our Chief Executive Of ficer in 2019. Prior to her current role, she served as chief financial of ficer and chief strategic transformation  
officer responsible for overseeing all aspects of strategic transformation and growth, digital and technology , global finance, investor relations, enterprise risk and  
compliance, integration management and Best Buy Health. Ms. Barry joined Best Buy in 1999 and has held a variety of financial and operational roles within the  
organization, both in the field and at corporate. Her prior roles include: the company’ s chief strategic growth of ficer and the interim leader of Best Buy’ s services  
organization from 2015 until 2016; senior vice president of domestic finance from 2013 to 2015; vice president, chief financial of ficer and business development  
of our home business group from 2012 to 2013; and vice president, finance of the home customer solutions group from 2010 to 2012. Prior to Best Buy , Ms.  
Barry worked at Deloitte & Touche LLP . Ms. Barry serves on the board of directors for Domino’ s Pizza Inc. and the board of trustees for the College of St.  
Benedict. She also serves on the executive committee for the Business Roundtable, Business Council, Retail Industry Leaders Association, and the Minnesota  
Business Partnership.
 
Matt Bilunas  is our Chief Financial Of ficer, appointed in 2019. In this role, he is responsible for overseeing all aspects of global finance and strategic planning, as  
well as audit, procurement and financial services. Since joining Best Buy in 2006, Mr . Bilunas has served in a variety of financial leadership roles, both in the field  
and at corporate. He started as a territory finance director in Los Angeles and has worked in the company’ s domestic and international businesses. Mr . Bilunas  
has been a key finance leader during Best Buy’ s transformation. Prior to his current role, he was senior vice president of enterprise and merchandise finance  
since 2017; vice president, finance for category , e-commerce and marketing from 2015 to 2017; and vice president, category finance from 2014 until 2015. He  
also has held finance roles in retail, e-commerce and marketing. Before Best Buy , he worked at Carlson Inc., NRG Energy Inc., Bandag Inc. and KPMG. Mr . 
Bilunas serves on the boards of the Children’ s Hospital of Minnesota and Genesco Inc., a retailer of branded footwear and accessories.
 
Jason Bonfig was appointed our Chief Merchandising Of ficer in 2019. In this role, he oversees all elements of merchandising and product category  
management for Best Buy’ s core U.S. business, including demand planning, buying, pricing and promotional planning. He also leads the company’ s Exclusive  
Brands private-label team. Mr . Bonfig has served in merchant roles for the company for over 20 years. Prior to his current role, Mr . Bonfig served in the positions  
of chief category of ficer – computing, mobile, gaming, health and wellness, accessories and exclusive brands from 2018 to 2019; senior vice president –  
computing, mobile, tablets, wearables, printing and accessories from 2014 to 2018. Mr . Bonfig also held merchant-related roles since joining the company in  
1999. He serves on the board of the Best Buy Foundation.
 
20Damien Harmon has served as our Executive V ice President, Omnichannel since 2021 and is responsible for establishing a dedicated operations plan that  
enhances the company’ s ability to create seamless experiences for our customers. He oversees all of its various service of ferings in stores, online and in  
customers’  homes. In his role, Mr . Harmon leads the Geek Squad, a national tech-support organization with more than 20,000 Agents dedicated to helping  
customers learn about and enjoy their technology . Mr. Harmon previously served as president, operations from 2020 to 2021 and senior vice president of  
workforce design from 2019 to 2020. Mr . Harmon first joined Best Buy as a general manager in 2005 and held various leadership positions in store operations,  
international operations and store leadership, including vice president of retail operations and services. Before rejoining Best Buy in 2019, Mr . Harmon spent four  
years at Bridgestone Americas Inc., where he served as president of GCR Tires from 2017 to 2018 and chief operating of ficer at Bridgestone Tires from 2016 to  
2017. Mr . Harmon serves on the boards of the Petlove Foundation and the Best Buy Foundation.
 
Todd G. Hartman was appointed General Counsel in 2019 and has also served as Chief Risk Of ficer since 2017. In this role, he is responsible for the company’ s 
legal activities and its global risk program. He also serves as corporate secretary . Mr. Hartman joined Best Buy in 2006. He most recently served as chief risk and  
compliance of ficer, overseeing enterprise data security , customer data privacy , enterprise risk management, global security , business continuity/disaster recovery , 
internal investigations, crisis response management and compliance and ethics from 2017 to 2019. He continues to lead the risk functions in his current role. Mr . 
Hartman previously was Best Buy’ s deputy general counsel from 201 1 to 2017. Before that, he served as the company’ s chief compliance of ficer and vice  
president of strategic alliances. Prior to joining Best Buy , Mr. Hartman was a partner at Minneapolis law firm Robins Kaplan. He serves as chair of the Best Buy  
Foundation and on the board of the Guthrie Theater .
 
Kamy Scarlett was appointed our Executive V ice President, Human Resources in 2017 and she also assumed responsibility for Best Buy Canada in 2021. In  
this role, she oversees talent development and the health and well-being of the more than 90,000 Best Buy employees worldwide. She also served as our  
president, U.S. retail stores from 2019 until 2020, and was responsible for the execution and operation of all domestic Best Buy store locations. Ms. Scarlett  
joined Best Buy in 2014 as senior vice president of retail and chief human resources of ficer for Best Buy Canada, serving in that role until 2017. She was  
responsible for sales and profits in more than 180 stores in addition to enacting the human resources and talent management strategies for the company . She  
has served in a variety of retail operations, marketing and human resources leadership roles since beginning her career in retail more than 30 years ago. Prior to  
joining Best Buy , Ms. Scarlett was the chief operating of ficer from 2012 to 2014 at Grafton-Fraser Inc., a leading Canadian retailer of men’ s apparel. She also  
previously held leadership roles at Loblaw Cos., Hudson’ s Bay Co. and Dylex Inc. Ms. Scarlett previously served on the board of directors of Floor & Decor , a 
specialty retailer of hard surface flooring.
 
Mathew R. W atson  was appointed our Senior V ice President, Controller and Chief Accounting Of ficer in 2017. He previously served as our vice president,  
controller and chief accounting of ficer from 2015 until his current role. Mr . Watson is responsible for our controllership, financial operations and external reporting  
functions. Mr . Watson has served in the role of vice president, finance - controller since 2014. Prior to that role, he was vice president - finance, domestic  
controller from 2013 to 2014. Mr . Watson was also senior director , external reporting and corporate accounting from 2010 to 2013 and director , external reporting  
and corporate accounting beginning in 2007. Prior to joining us in 2005, Mr . Watson worked at KPMG from 1995 to 2005. He serves on the boards of directors of  
Achieve Twin Cities and the Best Buy Foundation.

- Indications of reporting compliance (Exchange Act filings and Interactive Data Files), and that the company is not a shell company.
- Documents incorporated by reference: portions of the 2023 Definitive Proxy Statement for Part III.
- Safe harbor cautionary statement for forward-looking statements under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995.
- Table of Contents outlining Parts I–IV, including Business, Risk Factors, MD&A, Market Risk, Financial Statements, Controls and Procedures, and other standard 10-K items.
- Item 1. Business: Company overview—incorporated in Minnesota (1966); purpose to enrich lives through technology; vision to personalize and humanize technology solutions; operations in the U.S. and Canada.
- Reportable segments: Domestic (U.S. and Best Buy Health) and International (Canada). Domestic brands and domains include Best Buy, Best Buy Ads, Best Buy Business, Best Buy Health, CST, Current Health, Geek Squad, Lively, Magnolia, Pacific Kitchen and Home, TechLiquidators, Yardbird, and related websites; International brands include Best Buy, Best Buy Mobile, Geek Squad, and bestbuy.ca. Mexico stores closed by end of Q1 FY22.
- Recent acquisitions (FY22): Current Health Ltd. and Yardbird Furniture.
- Operations model: omnichannel platform (online, in-store, in-home); centrally managed merchandising, pricing, supply chain, digital, marketing, and support functions; standardized store procedures with localized flexibility; distinct leadership and operations for Best Buy Health supported by enterprise capabilities.
- Merchandise and services organized into six revenue categories:
  1) Computing and Mobile Phones (computers, peripherals, mobile, networking, tablets, wearables),
  2) Consumer Electronics (imaging, health/fitness, home theater, portable audio, smart home),
  3) Appliances (large and small),
  4) Entertainment (drones, gaming, media, toys, VR, software),
  5) Services (consultation, delivery, design, health services, installation, memberships, repair, setup, tech support, warranties),
  6) Other (baby, food/beverage, luggage, outdoor living, sporting goods).

top5_chunks.summary:
- Executive leadership profiles:
  - Damien Harmon, Executive Vice President, Omnichannel (since 2021): leads seamless customer experience across stores, online, and in-home; oversees Geek Squad (20,000 Agents); prior roles at Best Buy and Bridgestone; serves on Petlove Foundation and Best Buy Foundation boards.
  - Todd G. Hartman, General Counsel (since 2019) and Chief Risk Officer (since 2017): oversees legal, global risk, data security, privacy, business continuity, investigations, crisis response, and ethics; former deputy general counsel and chief compliance officer; chairs Best Buy Foundation and serves on Guthrie Theater board.
  - Kamy Scarlett, Executive Vice President, Human Resources (since 2017) and head of Best Buy Canada (since 2021): responsible for talent and well-being of 90,000+ employees; former president of U.S. retail stores; prior leadership at Grafton-Fraser, Loblaw, Hudson’s Bay, and Dylex; former Floor & Decor director.
  - Mathew R. Watson, Senior Vice President, Controller and Chief Accounting Officer (since 2017): leads controllership, financial operations, and external reporting; progressive finance roles at Best Buy since 2005; previously at KPMG; serves on boards of Achieve Twin Cities and Best Buy Foundation.

- Market for common stock and dividends:
  - BBY trades on NYSE.
  - Regular quarterly dividend initiated in 2004; increased to $0.92 per share on March 2, 2023; future dividends contingent on financial and other factors.
  - 1,955 holders of record as of March 15, 2023.

- Share repurchases:
  - $5.0 billion authorization approved February 28, 2022 (replacing prior $5.0 billion program); no expiration.
  - Fiscal 2023: repurchased and retired 11.8 million shares for $1.0 billion.
  - Fiscal 2023 Q4: 7,138,475 shares repurchased at an average $76.91; $4.125 billion remained authorized at quarter end.
